none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Constrained minimization of a convex differentiable function f over a nonempty compact convex set C. The gradient is L-Lipschitz on C, with L>0. Strong convexity of f is not assumed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: A query Sum.inl x returns ∇f(x) for every x∈C, at every call index and every seed. There is no gradient error or stochastic noise assumption; responses must be exact.

oracle.label: linear_minimization
oracle.details: A query Sum.inr g returns an exact minimizer of ⟨g,x⟩ over C for every direction g, call index, and seed. Selection among minimizers may vary. Each gradient or linear-minimization query counts as one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/UniformlyConvexHolder.lean: spec.admissible, Sum.inr clause; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: C has diameter at most D>0 and is uniformly convex with parameters a>0 and q>3: tx+(1−t)y+a t(1−t)‖x−y‖^q z∈C for x,y∈C, t∈[0,1], and ‖z‖≤1. A global Hölder error bound holds: for every x∈C there exists y∈argmin_C f with ‖x−y‖≤c(f(x)−f*)^(1/r), where c>0 and r>2. Public information consists of E, L, and a feasible x0; D,a,q,c,r,ε are not public algorithm inputs.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/UniformlyConvexHolder.lean: UniformlyConvexSet; Public; Params; spec.publicInput; spec.valid; spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output must belong to C and satisfy f(output)−f*≤ε, where ε>0 and f* is attained on C.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the ε objective-gap guarantee must hold almost surely under the output probability law, rather than merely in expectation.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: This specializes smooth constrained convex optimization through the joint assumptions of power-type uniform convexity of the feasible set with q>3 and a global Hölder error bound with r>2. These geometric and growth restrictions distinguish it from the basic smooth convex benchmark. No proved results or budgets were supplied, so no rate comparison was performed.
